title: The edge of the water
subtitle: Three studies from a fictional tidal observatory
purpose: Direct close looking through a fictional exhibition and give the visitor an observation task.

criteria: Use distinct opening, orientation, looking, index, comparison and closing roles.
Keep the print captions, dates, dimensions and observation tasks editable.

blocks.label: SHORELINE ROOM / STUDY NOTES

illustration.alt: A pale horizontal band above dark teal water ends in three descending steps.
illustration.caption: Low Bank. A continuous upper band breaks into steps.

blocks.lead: At the shoreline, the same mark can read as a boundary, a trace or an opening. Three study prints invite a second look at what the water leaves behind.

blocks.text: Enter from the dry side. The prints are arranged from a single cut to a sequence of overlapping marks. Stand back first, then move close enough to see where a contour loses its sharpness.
The room follows a low bank imagined for this exhibition. No print records a measured tide or an actual location. The route moves from an overall view into details, then returns to the whole group.

blocks.alt: Two offset bands face each other across an opening that widens to the right.
blocks.caption: Slack Water. Two edges open around a central gap.
blocks.side_text: The entrance print gives the eye a long horizontal line to follow. Its break is the first question to carry into the room: which edge are you following when the line disappears?

blocks.text: Low Bank sets a pale band against dark water. The band has a clean edge at left and breaks into small steps at right. The change can be read before the print is seen up close.

blocks.alt: A pale horizontal band above dark teal water ends in three descending steps.
blocks.caption: Low Bank. A continuous upper band breaks into steps.

blocks.text: Keep your gaze on the point where the long band ends. The next mark turns downward. It belongs to the same surface, even though it points in a different direction.
Dimensions describe the fictional studies, not the size of their reproductions on these pages. The three prints are shown in reading order around the room.
Slack Water puts two edges near each other without joining them. The narrow gap becomes visible at the center, then widens toward the right.

blocks.alt: Two offset bands face each other across an opening that widens to the right.
blocks.caption: Slack Water. Two edges open around a central gap.

blocks.text: Return Mark holds the same opening near its lower edge. The gap now points back toward the route you have walked. Compare where the pale strip ends before comparing color.

blocks.alt: A pale strip doubles back along the lower edge of a dark opening.
blocks.caption: Return Mark. A pale strip turns back below the opening.

blocks.text: On the next walk, choose one edge and follow it until it disappears. Notice whether its return changes the direction of your gaze.

items: Find a sharp edge and a fading edge.
Describe what separates them without naming a color.
Return to the entrance print and apply the same description.

blocks.text: An edge is easier to remember when you can say where it changes.
